tagline: Along the Kansas line from Edison to the Missouri.
intro: US 136 starts at Edison, a village named for the postmaster's boy, and keeps close to the Kansas line the whole way across. At Alma it runs by the northwest end of Harlan County Reservoir, the lake dammed on the Republican River after the flood of 1935, then goes on through Red Cloud, Hebron, Fairbury and Beatrice toward the Missouri.

The Homestead Act runs through it. Daniel Freeman, the first homesteader to file under the act, staked his claim at a New Year's Eve party in Brownville, and the national park five miles west of Beatrice takes in some of the first acres claimed. Brownville itself, once the largest town in Nebraska Territory, lost its river trade to the railroads.

moments.title: Red Cloud
moments.text: Willa Cather grew up in a rented frame house just west of downtown, and the town went into My Ántonia as Black Hawk.

moments.title: Rock Creek Station
moments.text: Wagon ruts still cut the ground at this Oregon Trail stop, where the toll bridge charged what a wagon could pay and a young James Hickok shot its builder in 1861.

moments.title: Brownville Bridge
moments.text: The highway leaves Nebraska on a 1939 truss bridge over the Missouri, one eight-foot lane each way and no shoulders.
